name: exploratory timing of first human BACK and semantic correction
interpretation: Humans typically reconsider after a small amount of forward exploration (median 3 clicks). Point estimates suggest somewhat larger semantic correction after more prior exploration, but target-matched uncertainty barely includes zero; additional benefit from long deferral is therefore not established.
boundary: Post-hoc exploratory analysis of AP-RS4 human finished paths.
Timing is measured in forward hyperlink actions, not reading time or cognitive context chunks.
Does not establish that delaying reconsideration causally improves navigation or comprehension.
